content.value_statement: Angular teams need clear state choices as apps grow. This skill provides practical patterns for Signals, NgRx, SignalStore, ComponentStore, and RxJS migration.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to use local, shared, global, server, URL, and form state.
Provides Signal service examples for component and shared Angular state.
Shows NgRx Store, actions, reducers, selectors, effects, and component usage.
Demonstrates NgRx SignalStore and ComponentStore patterns for feature state.
Covers migration from BehaviorSubject services to Angular Signals.
Shows how to bridge Signals and RxJS with Angular interop utilities.
limitations: Does not inspect a project automatically or run Angular tests.
Does not cover non-Angular frameworks or React state libraries.
Example API endpoints are placeholders and need project-specific services.
Advanced architectural choices still require review against team constraints.

use_cases.title: Choose a State Strategy
use_cases.description: Compare Signals, SignalStore, ComponentStore, and NgRx for an Angular feature before implementation.

use_cases.title: Modernize Legacy State
use_cases.description: Plan a migration from BehaviorSubject services to signal-based services with clear read and write APIs.
use_cases.target_user: Frontend leads maintaining older Angular apps

use_cases.title: Structure Enterprise Stores
use_cases.description: Design actions, reducers, selectors, effects, and component bindings for complex app-wide state.
use_cases.target_user: Teams using NgRx in larger Angular applications

prompt_templates.title: Pick the Right Pattern
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me choose an Angular state management pattern for this feature: [describe feature]. Compare Signals, SignalStore, ComponentStore, and NgRx.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Signal Service
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a signal-based Angular service for [state domain]. Include readonly state, computed values, loading state, errors, and update methods.

prompt_templates.title: Plan an NgRx Feature Slice
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an NgRx feature design for [domain]. Include actions, reducer shape, selectors, effects, and component integration notes.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor a Legacy Store
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Angular state pattern and propose a migration to Signals or NgRx SignalStore. Explain risks, steps, and testing priorities.

output_examples.input: I need state for a product list with filters, loading, and server refresh.
output_examples.output: A recommendation to use SignalStore, with state shape, computed filtered products, load methods, and component usage guidance.

output_examples.input: My app uses BehaviorSubject services for user session state.
output_examples.output: A migration plan that replaces writable subjects with private signals, readonly accessors, computed selectors, and explicit update methods.

output_examples.input: We need global cart and user state across many Angular routes.
output_examples.output: An NgRx structure with feature slices, actions, selectors, effects, and integration points for route-level components.

best_practices: Keep state local until multiple features need the same data.
Use computed values for derived state instead of storing duplicates.
Separate server loading, success, and error states from UI-only state.
anti_patterns: Do not globalize simple component state without a clear sharing requirement.
Do not mutate signal values directly outside controlled update methods.
Do not mix Signals and RxJS without a clear ownership boundary.

faq.question: Does this skill generate complete Angular stores?
faq.answer: It provides patterns and examples that can guide complete stores, but project services and tests must be adapted locally.

faq.question: When should I use NgRx instead of Signals?
faq.answer: Use NgRx when state spans many features, requires effects, or benefits from actions, reducers, selectors, and devtools.

faq.question: Can it help migrate from BehaviorSubject?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes a migration pattern that replaces BehaviorSubject state with private writable signals and readonly accessors.

faq.question: Does it cover server state?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows HTTP loading, error handling, optimistic updates, and RxJS bridging for server-backed Angular state.

faq.question: Is this skill limited to Angular Signals?
faq.answer: No. It also covers NgRx Store, NgRx SignalStore, RxJS ComponentStore, and interop between Signals and Observables.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, or Claude Code use this skill?
faq.answer: Yes. The report declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.
